issues.legal_issue: A donor may transfer ownership of property by gift while reserving possession, management, and enjoyment for the donor’s lifetime.
material_facts: The donor executed a registered deed gifting her share in property to her children.
The deed transferred ownership to the children but reserved the donor’s management, possession, and income during her lifetime.
The property was not restricted in its enjoyment to the donor personally.
issues.conclusion: The reservation of possession and enjoyment did not make the transfer of ownership ineffective.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6 of the Transfer of Property Act permits transfer of property of any kind except as specified, and Section 6(d) did not apply because enjoyment of the property was not restricted to the donor personally. Ownership may be gifted while possession and enjoyment are reserved for the donor’s lifetime.

rule.if: gift_transfer_dispute and donor_transferred_ownership and donor_reserved_lifetime_enjoyment and property_not_restricted_to_donor_personally

predicates.gift_transfer_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether a transfer of property by gift was effective.
predicates.donor_transferred_ownership: The donor’s deed transferred ownership of the property to the donee.
predicates.donor_reserved_lifetime_enjoyment: The donor retained possession, management, or enjoyment of the property for the donor’s lifetime.
predicates.property_not_restricted_to_donor_persona: The property was not of a kind whose enjoyment was restricted personally to the donor.

issues.definition: When a donor transfers ownership but keeps lifetime possession or enjoyment of property that is not restricted personally to the donor, the reservation does not invalidate the ownership transfer.

issues.legal_issue: A minor can accept a beneficial, non-onerous gift, and acceptance may be inferred from the circumstances without express acceptance or delivery of possession.
material_facts: The donor gifted property to her minor son, who was sixteen years old, and her four-year-old daughter.
The gift was beneficial and was not burdened by an obligation.
The donor was the minor son’s mother and guardian, and the father, who also lived with the family, knew of the gift.
The son knew of the gift and did not repudiate it after attaining majority.
The donor retained possession and enjoyment during her lifetime, and the donee did not take possession or have his name entered in official records.
issues.conclusion: The circumstances established acceptance of the gift by or on behalf of the minor; express acceptance and delivery of possession were not necessary.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 122 and 127 of the Transfer of Property Act recognize acceptance by or on behalf of a donee and the capacity of a minor to accept a non-onerous gift; Section 11 of the Contract Act makes a minor incompetent to contract but does not prevent the minor from receiving property. A gift from a parent to a child carries a presumption of acceptance, which may be inferred from knowledge and silence or conduct showing no repudiation. The Court relied on Firm of Ganeshdas Bhiwaraj v. Suryabhan, Munni Kunwar v. Madan Gopal, Sundar Bai v. Anandi Lal, Ponnuchami Servai v. Balasubramanian, Vannathi Valappil Janaki v. Puthiya Purayil Paru, Shankuntala Devi v. Amar Devi, and Narayani Bhanumathi v. Lalitha Bhai.

rule.if: gift_acceptance_dispute and gift_made_to_minor_child_by_parent and gift_is_beneficial_and_nononerous and minor_or_guardian_knew_of_gift and gift_not_repudiated_after_majority

predicates.gift_acceptance_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether a gift was accepted by or on behalf of its donee.
predicates.gift_made_to_minor_child_by_parent: A parent made the gift to the parent’s minor child.
predicates.gift_is_beneficial_and_nononerous: The gift conferred a benefit without burdening the donee with an obligation.
predicates.minor_or_guardian_knew_of_gift: The minor donee or the minor’s guardian knew of the gift.
predicates.gift_not_repudiated_after_majority: After attaining majority, the donee did not reject or repudiate the gift.

issues.definition: Where a parent makes a beneficial, non-onerous gift to a minor child, knowledge of the gift and its non-repudiation after majority support finding acceptance by or for the child.

issues.legal_issue: A completed and accepted gift cannot be revoked unilaterally by the donor except on a ground permitted by law.
material_facts: The gift was executed and accepted in 1945.
The donee attained majority and did not repudiate the gift.
The donor later executed a cancellation deed and a will dealing with the gifted property.
The circumstances did not establish a permitted ground for revoking the gift.
issues.conclusion: The donor could not cancel the completed gift or bequeath the gifted property by will.
issues.legal_principle: Section 126 of the Transfer of Property Act permits suspension or revocation in specified circumstances, including an agreed specified event not dependent on the donor’s will, or grounds on which a contract could be rescinded other than want or failure of consideration. Otherwise, a validly executed gift cannot be revoked.

rule.if: gift_revocation_dispute and gift_validly_completed_and_accepted and donor_attempted_unilateral_revocation and no_permitted_revocation_ground

predicates.gift_revocation_dispute: The proceeding concerns an attempt to revoke a gift.
predicates.gift_validly_completed_and_accepted: The gift was validly executed and accepted by or on behalf of the donee.
predicates.donor_attempted_unilateral_revocation: The donor attempted to cancel the gift without the donee’s agreement.
predicates.no_permitted_revocation_ground: No agreed qualifying event or other legally permitted ground for revocation was established.

issues.definition: A donor’s unilateral attempt to revoke a completed and accepted gift is ineffective when no permitted ground for revocation is established.
